name: Roskilde University
overview:
IMPORTANT - Additional Program Requirements


Students must have a minimum 785 on the Tepitech at the moment of the International Jury to be eligible for this destination


__________________________________________________________________________________


Roskilde University is a public university with an enrollment of 8,200 students.


It is divided into six departments:

  • Communication, Business and Information Technologies (CBIT)
  • Culture and Identity (CUID)
  • Environmental, Social and Spatial Change (ENSPAC)
  • Psychology and Educational Studies (PAES)
  • Systems and Models (NSM)
  • Society and Globalization (ISG)


The campus is located 5 km from downtown Roskilde.


Roskilde University is a very international university and receives a large number of foreign students each semester. Hearing Danish mix with English is common in the hallways of the university.


Roskilde University is also very well known in Denmark for its innovation, manifested in particular by its pedagogy and the various projects it supports.


For travel advice issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Denmark, click here.
administrative:
Application dossier


Once the IAFF office has sent your nomination, the partner university will contact you directly by email to start your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see EMEA Teams channel for each application deadline).


If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


To be completed with your Epitech bachelor campus administration during the registration period for Tech4 (usually in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


Visa


For European students, a valid passport/ national ID card is sufficient to travel to Europe (exception for the UK).


For non-Europeans students or students with a non-European citizenship, please check the immigration office of the host country to check the visa process and fees.


Students in France can use this website: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/


Insurance


For European students


The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM in French) is nominative and individual. This card certifies your rights to the Health Insurance in Europe. To obtain your card, log in to your Ameli account at least two months before your departure. It is free of charge and will be sent to your place within two weeks. You can also download it online.


For more information: https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/europe-international/protection-sociale-etranger/etudes-etranger


For non-European students


You must register for a private health insurance to cover your full stay. Please check with your parents, bank, or any private insurance company for more information depending on the wanted coverage.


Please register via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ariane) platform to be aware of any news (terrorist attack, tsunami, earthquake…) in your host country for French citizens only:

https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/ public / login.html


4. When you arrive in Denmark


You have 6 months after you arrive in Denmark to ask for a personal identification number, also called CPR number. In Denmark they use this number for everything: health, bank, phone number...


Please do the necessary procedure as soon as possible and not wait until the last minute.

https://www.mitid.dk/en-gb/


Campus life


For further information on the university and life in Denmark, see the student guide:

http://www.e-pages.dk/roskildeuniversitet/290/html5/

courses:
You must obtain 30 ECTS credits per semester, i.e. 60 ECTS credits for the year.


At Roskilde, you will follow two semesters of Computer Science in the Communication, Business & Information Technologies department.


Academic year:

  • Autumn semester: 01 September – 31 January
  • Spring semester: 01 February – 30 June


Orientation days:

  • Autumn semester: Last 2 weeks of August
  • Spring semester: Last 2 weeks of January


It is highly recommended to attend the orientation days as they will provide valuable information about courses and student life, as well as introduce you to your classmates.


Here are the lists of classes and projects offered:


Autumn

  • Computer Science - Bachelor level for exchange students
  • Computer Science - Master level for exchange students


Spring

  • Computer Science - Bachelor level for exchange students
  • Computer Science - Master level for exchange students


Of the 30 credits per semester, 15 are for a compulsory project linked to a required class that counts for 10 credits. The remaining 5 credits relate to an elective class, which is free to choose from among several themes that change every year.


This year we had the choice of Big Data, Robotics, or UX Design.


You must complete the project below to obtain 15 ECTS:


CS-SMP – Subject module project in Computer Science and computer modules for 45 ECTS.
cost:
You should plan a budget of DKK 8000 per month or € 1,070/month.


  • Round trip airfare: Between € 150 and € 300 (depending on the period, the company, etc.)
  • Insurance: European "Améli" insurance card (free)
  • Housing: € 560 / DKK 3300–4200
  • (If you live on campus, the rent will include utilities such as internet, laundry, electricity, heat, and water, and still will rarely exceed DKK 4200–4300)
  • Food: DKK 1500–2000 / Between € 200 and € 270 per month
  • (It is more expensive than in France. For example: the cheapest package of pasta costs € 1, a small jar of Nutella is € 4.50–5, a pizza is € 4–5, a box of cereal is € 3.5–4.5)
  • Books: DKK 450–600 (€ 60–80) / Between € 60 and € 90 per month
  • (However, certain books are available to students online)
  • Transportation: DKK 300–1100 (€ 40–150)
  • (Depending on whether you live on campus or in the city. Note that if you live on campus you will hardly need to take public transport, unless you want to go to Copenhagen or Roskilde. A round trip from campus to Copenhagen would cost around € 16–20)
  • Sports Center: € 30 per semester


These prices are indicative, and may vary.
